newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty slips vs basket, O/N near lombard.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty slips vs basket, O/N near lombard.

text.p: The zloty eased slightly in early trade as banks rebuilt currency positions cut on Wednesday, but dealers said it would not break out of its weeks-old range around resistance at 1.5 percent from parity.
Dealers said controversy over Poland's budget deficit plans for 1998 had not so far affected the zloty, which seemed destined to return to central bank enforced resistance levels.
"Players started short and rebuilt currency positions, depressing the zloty, but the Polish currency should return to 1.5 percent later today," said one Polish bank dealer.
At 0915 GMT the zloty was quoted at 1.46/1.43 percent from parity, softer than the opening's 1.53/1.49 percent.
It was at 3.2433/43 to the dollar, down from 3.2395/05 at 0710 GMT and at 1.8803/08 to the mark from 1.8795/05.

On Wednesday Finance Minister Marek Belka said foreign direct investment, a tight monetary policy and a leaner 1998 budget gap, seen at or below 2.0 percent of GDP, would stop the fast deterioration of Poland's current account balance.
Ealier in the week the central bank's deputy president said that unless Poland balanced its budget next year, it would be on the road to a financial crisis.

The money market remained short-of-cash with only two working days left in the monthly required reserve period, which ends on June 29, with one-day rates lingering around the 25-percent lombard rate, dealers said.

Some said however, that overnight rates were inflated as many players had free cash, but were reluctant to place it, knowing that banks which were short had to buy at any price to square positions before the end of the reserve account.
At 0930 GMT O/N rates were at 23.00/24.50 percent, down from 23.80/24.60 at 0630 GMT. Tomorrow/next were at 22.60/23.60 percent against 23.70/24.50. -- Wojciech Moskwa +48 22 653 9700
